narration: Welcome to the Decorative Arts gallery. Here we have the Painted Hand Fan, accession number NM 89.1/6, a beautiful example of 18th‑to‑19th‑century craftsmanship from the Deccan region of North India. The fan’s wooden frame, measuring about 45 centimetres when open, is covered in delicate floral pigment, a design typical of the attendants who would cool a seated noble in a Mughal or Deccan court. While the exact workshop or court of origin has not yet been researched, the fan’s elegance speaks to the refined artistry of that era. If you’d like to learn more about similar court accessories, feel free to ask.
